title: Annotatio IV §.V close: On to later ages via early Fathers; both sides cite two things, spiritual mode only — stop before §.VI
pass_a_gloss: So that by this very thing, after the true Doctrine concerning the Sacred Supper has been drawn from the origin through the course of the whole first Christian age, we may now with ready foot stretch on to the succeeding ages, the testimonies of the first Fathers about to build and confirm the same. Indeed we know well that we are lightened in this labor by the excellent industry of certain Protestant Doctors demolishing Pontifical Novelties about the Sacred Supper — John Oecolampadius, Philip Melanchthon, Martin Chemnitz, Daniel Chamier, and most lately John Cosin and Joh. Guil. Baier; yet lest this little Historical work of ours gape open, we shall not grudge to call from these very Authors at least two, or at most three, witnesses for the truth of each of the purer ages, in whose mouth this truth too may stand unmoved — if first we warn this one thing: that the named collectors of the Ancients’ Testimonies, though devoted to diverse Protestant sects, nonetheless brought nearly the same from the five earlier ages especially, doubtless for this cause, or could not but bring them, that in them the thing itself alone is found inculcated — i.e. presence and participation of two things, celestial and terrestrial, Signified and Sign, in the lawful use of the Sacred Supper — apart from any mode of presence and participation of the other thing (the Signified), or with its sole, merely spiritual mode, conceded by both Protestant parties.
pass_b_english: Doctrine now traced from the origin through the whole first Christian age — we may step on to later ages with early Fathers to confirm it.
Protestant collectors (Oecolampadius, Melanchthon, Chemnitz, Chamier, Cosin, Baier) already demolished Pontifical novelties; we still take two or three witnesses per purer age from them.

Both sides cite nearly the same from the first five ages: presence of two things (celestial & terrestrial / Signified & Sign) with only the spiritual mode of the Signified conceded. Stop before §.VI (second century: Ignatius, Justin, Irenaeus).
source_text: Ut hôc ipsô, post deductam ab origine, per totius primi Seculi Christiani decursum, veram de S. Cœna Doctrinam, nunc promptô pede ad succedentia Secula liceat nobis pertendere, primorum Patrum testimoniis eandem adstructuris & confirmaturis. Equidem nos hâc operâ levatos per quorundam Protestantium Doctorum egregiam industriam, Pontificias Novitates, circa S. Cœnam demolientium, Joh. Oecolampadii, Philippi Melanchtonis, Martini Chemnitii, Danielis Chamieri, & novissimè Johannis Cosini nec non Joh. Guil. Bajeri, probè novimus; ne tamen Historica hæc Opella nostra hiulca evadat, haud gravabimur ex his ipsis Autoribus, singulorum seculorum saltem puriorum testes pro veritate, vel binos, vel ad summum tres, advocare, in quorum ore & hæc veritas immota perstet, si in antecessum hoc unicum monuerimus, nominatos Veterum Testimoniorum collectores, etsi diversæ Protestantium Sectæ addictos, eadem tamen propemodum ex quinque præsertim Seculis prioribus, hac proculdubio de causa adduxisse, vel non potuisse non adducere, quòd in iis res ipsa solummodò, i. e. duarum rerum, cœlestis & terrestris, Signati & Signi, in legitimo S. Cœnæ usu, præsentia & participatio, citra vel ullum præsentiæ & participationis rei alterius, Signati scil. modum, vel cum hujus solo, duntaxat spirituali modo, ab utraque Protestantium parte concesso, inculcare deprehenduntur.

lemmas.gloss: of two things, celestial and terrestrial

notes: Bridge to later ages; two things / spiritual mode; stop §.VI.
